name: GCSE English Literature (AQA 8702)

selected_options.modern_text: An Inspector Calls (JB Priestley) — drama route

material_vintage: AQA GCSE English Literature (8702) specification, Version 1.3 (28 September 2022; first teaching 2015, first exams 2017), itemised on 2026-09-22. Verified against AQA's own specification PDF (sections 3.1 Shakespeare/19th-century novel, 3.2 Modern texts and poetry, 3.3 Skills, 4.1-4.3 aims/assessment objectives/weightings) and against AQA's live subject-content pages for the current modern-texts list, confirming AO wording, the AO1 37.5% / AO2 42.5% / AO3 15% / AO4 5% overall weighting split, the 64-mark 1h45 Paper 1 (40%) and 96-mark 2h15 Paper 2 (60%) structure, that there is no non-exam assessment or Spoken Language component in Literature (unlike English Language 8700), and the current (non-retired) modern-texts and poetry-cluster option lists. Individual question mark splits (Section A/B extract questions 30+4 AO4, unseen poetry Q1 24 / Q2 8) are carried from the previously-verified AQA mark-scheme rubric (see source_notes) and not re-fetched line by line on this rebuild, so are flagged for re-verification against a live mark scheme. The Power and Conflict poem list (15 titles/poets) is written from established, stable AQA cluster content and is flagged for re-verification against the anthology page. Lesson explanations, paraphrase, context notes, model-paragraph structure and every practice/test scenario are original and written for this course; no set-text passage, poem or mark-scheme wording is reproduced beyond the brief, sub-eight-word quotations the copyright rule allows for in-copyright texts.
level_source: RQF Level 2 (GCSE, full grade range 1-9 / Foundation+Higher tiers covered), per Ofqual's Register of Regulated Qualifications listing for this specification
framework: AQA's six-level 'levels of response' ladder for every essay (Level 1 simple/narrative -> Level 6 critical/exploratory), assessing AO1 (response with references), AO2 (analyse language/form/structure), AO3 (context), and AO4 (technical accuracy, Shakespeare and modern-text essays only). Paper 1 Section A (Shakespeare) and Paper 2 Section A (modern text) are marked out of 34 (30 content marks across AO1/AO2/AO3 plus 4 separate AO4 marks); Paper 1 Section B (19th-century novel) and Paper 2 Section B (poetry comparison) are marked out of 30 with no separate AO4 component; Paper 2 Section C (unseen poetry) is marked out of 32, split Question 1 24 marks (AO1+AO2, single poem) and Question 2 8 marks (AO2 only, comparison of methods), with no AO3/context marks.
